_comment: HunyuanVideo 1.5 720p IMAGE-to-video, plus the 1080p SR distill as an optional second stage. This is the direct rival to 12_ltx23_i2v_audio.json - the keyframe locks the character design and the model animates it. Base pass plus the 1080p super-resolution distill, which is the template's optional second stage. Node 63 HunyuanVideo15SuperResolution re-conditions on the start image, 62 upscales the latent to 1920x1080, and 66 SplitSigmas hands the noised half to 71 and the clean half to 73. This writes TWO videos: the 720p base from node 42 and the 1080p from node 76. Slow - measure before reaching for it.
_notes: BASE-ONLY: delete nodes 60-76. Their only inputs from the base graph are node 35 (sampler latent), 10/11 (text), 8 (image), 9 (clip vision) and 3 (vae); nothing in 1-42 reads back from them. studio/_tools/video_engine_ab.py does this with its --sr flag.

NO AUDIO. This is the one hard capability regression against LTX: 12_ltx23_i2v_audio.json generates a synchronised audio track in the same pass (LTXVEmptyLatentAudio + LTXVAudioVAEDecode). HunyuanVideo 1.5 is video-only, so any pipeline that moves to it must source audio separately.

THE KEYFRAME GOES IN TWICE, and both matter. Node 20 start_image is the latent conditioning; node 9 CLIPVisionEncode via sigclip is a SEPARATE semantic conditioning path. Dropping the clip_vision_output leaves the graph runnable but weakens subject adherence - it is not optional in practice.

There is no strength knob. LTXVImgToVideoInplace exposes strength (1.0 = hold the keyframe exactly, 0.6-0.8 = let the model reinterpret); HunyuanVideo15ImageToVideo has no equivalent. Keyframe adherence is take-it-or-leave-it.
length must be 4n+1; 97 = 4.04s at 24fps, matching the LTX motion library exactly.
shift 7 is BOTH the Tencent table value for 720p_i2v AND the shipped template value - unlike t2v, where the two disagree. See 41_hunyuan_t2v.json notes.
NOT A BUG, COPIED DELIBERATELY: node 34 BasicScheduler reads the RAW model (2), not the shifted model (30). The shipped template wires it this way.
cfg 6 = two model evaluations per step, and the negative prompt on node 11 is LIVE (unlike qwen, and unlike cfg-distilled LTX). The template ships it empty.
SR block cost: it re-samples at 1920x1080 through a second 16 GB model. Expect the SR stage to dominate wall-clock and to force a full unload/reload of the base model on a 32 GB card.

THE SR STAGE IS MEASURED BROKEN - DO NOT SHIP ITS OUTPUT. Nodes 60-76 run LIVE in this graph and node 76 writes a _sr file on every execution, so the cost is paid whether or not anyone wanted it. A controlled test (samples/hunyuan/compare/sr_stage_isolated.png - the SAME Hunyuan clip with and without the stage) shows the 1920 SR output with a smeared face, lost eyes and a distorted mouth against a sharp 1280 bicubic control. It is not softer, it is destroyed, and destroyed at higher resolution - on the model OWN supported path at the shipped template settings. noise_augmentation 0.15 instead of 0.7 does not rescue it; it swaps the melt for a heavy teal cast with the identity replaced (samples/hunyuan/compare/sr_face_4way.png). Root cause not isolated. Until it is, take the base 1280 output and upscale conventionally, and see the BASE-ONLY note above for how to drop the block.
Both SaveVideo nodes fire: 42 writes the 720p base, 76 writes the 1080p.
If you only want the base, run 42_hunyuan_i2v.json - it is the same graph without this block.

inputs.text: A scene with gentle natural motion.
